rule: A creature's stats come from a band row keyed by (tier, level, zone, instance). The tier is raid (2), named (1) or trash (0), set by a data flag or by a name test (# prefix, capital first letter). Lookup order is exact zone and instance, then zone with instance 0, then 0 and 0. Each band stat is written only where the creature's own field is zero (zero means inherit); auto-scaling also requires HP, damage and core attributes to be zero. A level change resets the stats the band wrote (tracked as modify_stat_ entity variables) and re-applies the band. Damage is multiplied by a class-and-level factor over 220. Special abilities come from a string of id,value pairs separated by caret, applied only to creatures with none. Body size defaults to a race-and-gender table (6.0 for most), with two hard-coded overrides. Recolour is one tint id per row that selects one of seven RGB slot sets.

data_fields.name: band_resists_8
data_fields.unit: rating each (mr, cr, fr, pr, dr, corruption, physical)

data_fields.name: size_default_by_race
data_fields.unit: float model height (default 6.0 for most rows)

data_fields.name: tint_id
data_fields.unit: integer id; seven slots, RGB 0-255 each

keep: band table keyed by tier, level, zone and instance, with a fallback chain from exact zone to global
zero-means-inherit: a creature's own zero takes the band value; a set value is kept
level change: reset the band's own writes, then re-apply the band for the new level
tag string of id,value pairs for one swapped or added ability per named row
size as a model float, default by body from a table, with a fixed flag for special bodies
one tint id per row selecting a recolour set of seven slots
change: missing band row falls through to zero stats; fall back to nearest level in same tier and zone and fail loudly in dev
duplicate band keys dropped silently by emplace (first row wins); detect at load
static bake writes the npc_types row shared by all zones; bake per zone key or use the dynamic path only
class damage factors are code, not data; move to a data table
named-tier test uses upper-case first letter on a plain char; use an explicit data flag first and an unsigned char test
hard-coded sizes for two races in the constructor; make them data flags
donor size is model-only as far as read; keep hit reach as a separate engine field
look_test: Phone at 375 wide, four rows of one body shape with our own art or boxes: base member at size 1.0 and tint A; same body at size 1.25 and tint B; same at 1.25 and tint B with one swapped ability (a short lunge on the first hit); boss-gate variant at size 1.5, tint C, with a spurt move starting under 70 percent HP. Dom judges whether row 3 reads as same family, worse, rather than a new monster. Numbers are placeholders.
